stem.text: Determine whether \( f(x) = -4 + 4 e^{- 2 x} \) is the particular solution to the differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} = - 2 y - 8 \) with the initial condition \( f(0) = 0 \). Justify your answer.

answer_key.label: Yes. \( f^{\prime}(x) = -2\left(f(x) + 4\right) \) for every x, and \( f(0) = 0 \).

worked_solution.text: Differentiate the candidate: \( f^{\prime}(x) = - 8 e^{- 2 x} \).
Substitute into the right side: \( -2\left(f(x) + 4\right) = - 8 e^{- 2 x} \), which equals \( f^{\prime}(x) \) for every x, so f satisfies the differential equation.
Check the initial condition: \( f(0) = 0 \), which matches, so f is the particular solution.

options.label: No. \( f^{\prime}(x) \ne -2\left(f(x) + 4\right) \) for the candidate, so f is not a solution of the equation.
